properties.natural_language: Before invoking the RIPEMD-160 precompile via EDGE-CALLER-INVOKE-RIPEMD, the calling contract must provide data through evm.message.data at precompile address 0x03
After RIPEMD-160 execution completes, evm.output must contain exactly 32 bytes: 12 leading zero bytes followed by the 20-byte RIPEMD-160 hash digest
The RIPEMD-160 precompile must be deterministic: identical input data must always produce identical 32-byte output across all invocations
Before gas deduction for RIPEMD-160, the available gas must be checked against GAS_RIPEMD160 + GAS_RIPEMD160_WORD * ceil32(len(data)) / 32
After gas deduction, the system must be in either STATE-GAS-SUFFICIENT-RIPEMD or STATE-GAS-INSUFFICIENT-RIPEMD with no other outcome possible
Gas cost must scale linearly with input size: total_gas = base_cost + per_word_cost * ceil(len(data)/32), ensuring DoS resistance for large inputs
Before processing untrusted input from external callers via EDGE-EXTERNAL-HASH-INPUT, the precompile must accept arbitrary byte sequences without length restrictions
The RIPEMD-160 hash function must always produce exactly 20 bytes of output regardless of input length, which is then padded to 32 bytes
The hashlib RIPEMD-160 implementation must be available on all execution environments, and its output must conform to the RIPEMD-160 standard
Before verifying a single Merkle proof via EDGE-RECEIVE-PROOF, the external proof provider must supply a leaf value, generalized index, proof siblings, and expected root from a trusted source
Before root reconstruction, the proof length must equal get_generalized_index_length(index), ensuring the correct number of sibling hashes for the tree depth
After proof verification, the system must be in exactly one of STATE-PROOF-VALID or STATE-PROOF-INVALID with no ambiguous intermediate state
The Merkle root reconstruction must use the generalized index bits to determine left/right hash ordering at each level, ensuring positional integrity
Before multi-proof verification via EDGE-RECEIVE-MULTIPROOF, the external provider must supply leaf values, their generalized indices, helper proof nodes, and an expected root
After multi-proof verification completes, the system must reach STATE-MULTIPROOF-VALID or STATE-MULTIPROOF-INVALID, authenticating all leaves simultaneously
The helper indices computed by get_helper_indices must represent the minimal set of auxiliary nodes needed for root reconstruction, and len(proof) must equal len(helper_indices)
Before generalized index path resolution via EDGE-RECEIVE-PATH, the caller must provide a valid object access path and a corresponding SSZ type schema
After path resolution, the final generalized index must correctly encode the tree position via concat_generalized_indices for all nested path elements
Before dispatching to a precompile via EDGE-CALL-TO-LOOKUP, the target address must be checked against the PRE_COMPILED_CONTRACTS dictionary
After address lookup, exactly one of STATE-ADDRESS-IS-PRECOMPILE or STATE-ADDRESS-NOT-PRECOMPILE must be reached, with no ambiguity
After precompile execution via EDGE-EXEC-TO-RESULT, the result must be available in STATE-PRECOMPILE-RESULT-READY for the calling context
The PRE_COMPILED_CONTRACTS registry must be immutable at runtime: addresses 0x01 through 0x11 must always map to the same implementations
Dictionary lookup for precompile dispatch must be constant-time O(1) to prevent timing side-channel attacks that fingerprint precompile usage
Each precompile address must belong to exactly one cryptographic operation category, ensuring clear security classification
Before transaction type routing via EDGE-RECEIVE-TX, the transaction submitter must provide a valid EIP-2718 typed transaction envelope with a type byte
After RIP range check, the transaction type must be classified as either RIP (0x40-0x7f inclusive) or EIP (outside that range) with no overlap
The RIP reserved range must always be exactly 0x40 through 0x7f (64 values), and this range must not overlap with any EIP-defined transaction types
Before namespace authority validation, the transaction must first pass EIP-2718 compliance checks for typed envelope format
After namespace authority validation, a transaction type must either be recognized (STATE-TX-TYPE-VALID) or rejected as unknown (STATE-TX-TYPE-UNKNOWN)
Before routing a transaction by type at the L1/L2 boundary, the transaction context (L1 or L2) must be established
L1 nodes must never process RIP transaction types (0x40-0x7f) as valid EIP transaction types, maintaining strict namespace separation
Before attestation inclusion processing via EDGE-VALIDATOR-CREATES, the validator must create an attestation for a specific slot S in epoch N with valid attestation data
After inclusion window check, attestations within the window must be processable for inclusion, while those outside must be rejected
The inclusion window must extend until the last slot of epoch N+1, i.e., slot (N+2)*SLOTS_PER_EPOCH - 1, for an attestation created in epoch N
Before attestation validation via EDGE-RECEIVE-ATTESTATION, the attestation must arrive from a network peer with associated attestation data
After validation, attestations with valid target epochs (current or previous) must reach STATE-ATTESTATION-VALID, while others reach STATE-ATTESTATION-INVALID
Validation must enforce sequential checks: minimum slot requirement first, then target epoch check, with no bypass path
After processing a valid attestation, TIMELY_TARGET_FLAG must always be set regardless of inclusion delay, guaranteeing a non-zero baseline reward
Before gossip propagation evaluation via EDGE-RECEIVE-GOSSIP, the attestation must be received from a P2P gossip peer with valid attestation/aggregate data
After gossip condition evaluation, attestations within the extended window must be propagated, while stale attestations must be dropped without forwarding
Before optimistic block import, the block must be evaluated as an optimistic candidate: parent has execution enabled OR current_slot > block.slot + SAFE_SLOTS_TO_IMPORT_OPTIMISTICALLY (128)
After execution engine verification, the payload must transition to exactly one of VALID, NOT_VALIDATED, or INVALIDATED states
After invalidation, all descendants of the invalid block must be removed from fork choice and their attestation weights excluded from ancestor calculations
A NOT_VALIDATED payload can only transition to VALID or INVALIDATED, never back to NOT_VALIDATED or to any other state
Merge blocks within SAFE_SLOTS_TO_IMPORT_OPTIMISTICALLY window must NOT be imported optimistically, protecting against fork choice poisoning during initial transition
Before allowing any validator duties, the node must verify its head block is NOT in optimistic_roots set
While the node is in optimistic state, signing with DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER, DOMAIN_BEACON_ATTESTER, and DOMAIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE must be prohibited
Fork choice poisoning mitigation must ensure the honest chain can override a poisoned store when it achieves a higher justified checkpoint within the SAFE_SLOTS window
Before computing fork choice head with optimistic blocks, the fork choice tree must correctly track which blocks are in optimistic_roots
After pruning an invalid branch, fork choice must be recomputed with only valid and optimistic blocks remaining in STATE-FC-CLEANED
Re-orgs must never cross a justified checkpoint: if invalidation affects a justified checkpoint, the system must reach STATE-JUSTIFIED-CHECKPOINT-AFFECTED and handle accordingly
Before ceil32 alignment via EDGE-RECEIVE-MEM-SIZE, the gas calculator must provide a non-negative unsigned integer memory size value
After ceil32 processing, the output must be a multiple of 32 that is greater than or equal to the input value
Before Taylor exponential computation via EDGE-RECEIVE-EXP-PARAMS, the fee market must provide factor, numerator, and denominator with denominator > 0
After Taylor series convergence, the result must approximate factor * e^(numerator/denominator) using integer arithmetic with floor division
The Taylor series must always converge (terminate) because factorial denominator growth causes the accumulated numerator to reach zero for any finite input
Before byte-to-U32 conversion via EDGE-BYTES-TO-U32-INPUT, the cryptographic operation must provide raw bytes whose length is a multiple of 4
Round-trip conversion bytes->U32->bytes must produce identical output to input: le_uint32_sequence_to_bytes(le_bytes_to_uint32_sequence(x)) == x for all valid inputs
Before numeric validation via EDGE-RECEIVE-NUMBER, the validation component must provide a numeric value for primality or sign determination
After primality check, the number must be classified as either prime (no divisors found from 2 to sqrt(n)) or not prime (divisor found or n <= 1)
Sign determination must return exactly one of -1, 0, or +1, covering all possible numeric values with no gaps
Before genesis block creation, no blockchain must exist (STATE-NO-BLOCKCHAIN) and a valid genesis configuration JSON file must be available in assets/
After genesis block creation, the chain must have exactly one block (block 0) with correct state root computed from all pre-allocated accounts
The genesis block creation process must be deterministic: the same genesis configuration must always produce the same state root and block hash across all implementations
Before hex value parsing, the raw configuration must have been read from the genesis JSON file
After validation, all account addresses must be valid 20-byte values and all balances must be valid U256 values, or a parse error must halt initialization
Hex parsing must treat 0x-prefixed strings as hexadecimal and non-prefixed strings as decimal, with no ambiguity
Fork-specific header fields must be added cumulatively: post-Cancun includes blob fields AND withdrawals root AND base fee, not just blob fields
After fork type check, pre-London forks must NOT include base_fee_per_gas in the genesis header

Before processing a signing request via EDGE-RECEIVE-REQUEST, the validator client must submit an HTTP POST to /sign/:identifier with a JSON body containing bls_domain, data, fork, and genesis_validators_root
After successful signing, the response must be HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing the BLS signature as a hex string
After key lookup failure, the response must be HTTP 404; after parse/domain failure, the response must be HTTP 400
The signing flow must enforce sequential validation: parse body -> lookup key -> validate domain -> compute signature, with no bypass path to signature computation
BLS domain validation must restrict signing to only beacon_proposer, beacon_attester, and randao domains, rejecting all other values
Before any signing request is processed, the network boundary must authenticate the request and verify it is within rate limits
After authentication failure, the request must be rejected without reaching the key lookup or signing stages
Private keys must be stored in HSM/secrets manager at rest and zeroized from memory after signing operations complete
Communication channel must use TLS/HTTPS encryption; plaintext HTTP exposes signatures to eavesdropping risk
Rate limiting must be enforced on authenticated requests to prevent denial-of-service attacks against the signing service
Before API request validation via EDGE-RECEIVE-HTTP, the HTTP client must submit a request to the BLS remote signer endpoint
API validation must enforce sequential checks: HTTP method -> content type -> JSON parse -> required fields -> domain value -> hash format, with failure at any step terminating the chain
After invalid JSON parsing, the system must reach STATE-JSON-INVALID and never proceed to field validation
Before error classification via EDGE-ERROR-TRIGGER, the request processing pipeline must detect an error condition
After error classification, client errors must result in 400 or 404 responses, and server errors must result in 500 responses
All detected errors must be logged for operational monitoring regardless of error type or response code
Before Berlin hardfork activation via EDGE-PRE-BERLIN-OPERATION, the network must be operating under pre-Berlin consensus rules
After Berlin rules activation, the network must operate under Berlin consensus rules with all constituent EIPs active
Fork activation must be irreversible: once STATE-POST-BERLIN is reached, the network must never revert to pre-Berlin rules
Before block validation via EDGE-BLOCK-FROM-PEER, the block must be received from a network peer with complete block data
After fork status check, the correct rule set must be applied: pre-Berlin for blocks before fork block, Berlin rules for blocks at or after fork block
Block validation must always result in exactly one of STATE-BLOCK-VALID or STATE-BLOCK-INVALID, regardless of which rule set is applied
Before EIP aggregation via EDGE-EIP-SUBMISSION, individual EIP authors must submit their proposals for Berlin inclusion
After EIP aggregation, the Berlin specification must be finalized in eth1.0-specs with a complete list of all included changes
